items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There’s tuba players coming along, like Billy Butterfield and Bill Barber, who was the great one.

ctx.x: Take us back, if you will: Miles, John Lewis, 1949, Birth of the Cool. Is that the beginning of Third Stream? I always think of – it’s got tuba. It’s got french horn. Was that germ there? Or am I . . . ?
Of course, of course. That was beginning to happen. It’s also – right around the same time there are Gerry Mulligan’s octets and tentets. There’s tuba players coming
along, like Billy Butterfield and Bill Barber, who was the great one. And the softer colors of the horn and french horn were being discovered by almost everybody.
